Folks who oppose eating GMO crops just because they're GMO are missing the point. The crops themselves are no less safe, the GMO portion exists to ensure that specific pesticides work and to place patents on the crops. Both of those are abhorrent practices that may make the crops less safe to eat (in the case of some pesticides) and most certainly make them less safe to grow near (as Monsanto LOVES to sue farmers), but the simple fact that they're GMO doesn't inherently make crops more dangerous to anyone's health.

Lab grown meat will be the same thing, except likely better for us. For instance, some red meats such as bison contain Omega-3 Fatty Acids, making it FAR better than cow or chicken. Bison are, however, much more difficult and excessively dangerous to raise in food herds, so most Americans have to consume fish to get those same acids, which is itself becoming more and more dangerous due to mercury and other contaminants often found in unsafe levels in fish. Lab-grown bison meat (or GMO meat with similar characteristics) will be an absolute game-changer for the health of our population, who today exist on, as you said, meat that relies on excessive antibiotics/hormones and largely has the nutrition bred out for sheer weight.

Right now, I have to just guess what's GMO and what's not when I shop.

The environment and monoculture aren't problems where lab-grown meat is concerned. So, I see lab-grown meat and GMO crops as two separate issues.

Slaughtering animals for meat doesn't bother me, either. Humans are not the only animal that eats meat, after all.
